# joints.library: SpringForce

**Status:** Experimental (tier `future`). Aspirational vocabulary. It must parse and type-check; it is not linted or converted to C#.

## Summary

> The force the spring exerts along the line between its anchors, in newtons,
> signed so that a positive value pushes the anchors apart: Hooke's restoring
> term plus a damping term proportional to the rate of change of the length.
> (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooke%27s\_law)

### Line 163

**Source:** [stdlib/future/joints.library.plato, line 163](../../../../../stdlib/future/joints.library.plato#L163).

```plato

    //==
    // # Springs
    //
    // A spring joint is not a constraint: it exerts a FORCE and lets the integrator
    // decide what happens. That is why it takes a time step and produces an impulse
    // rather than being iterated — iterating a spring would multiply its stiffness
    // by the iteration count.
    //
    // A spring stiff enough to look rigid is stiff enough to be unstable at the
    // step sizes a real-time simulation uses; a joint that must be rigid should be
    // a `DistanceJoint` with equal bounds instead.

    // The force the spring exerts along the line between its anchors, in newtons,
    // signed so that a positive value pushes the anchors apart: Hooke's restoring
    // term plus a damping term proportional to the rate of change of the length.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooke%27s_law)
    SpringForce(joint: SpringJoint, extension: Number, lengthRate: Number): Number
        => -joint.Stiffness.Amount * extension - joint.Damping.Amount * lengthRate;
```
